subject: Exact-head CI pre-verification: one hard blocker found and FIXED; two load-sensitive flakes observed; the v6 gates are NOT wired into CI
instruction: Still no modification of golden.v6, the resolver classification, or the lineage. This entry records CI-path findings only.

qualityJobGates: npm run test:ci   = test:unit && test:contract && test:integration && test:architecture && test:stage12-package
whatCiActuallyRuns.requiredGates: both the quality and frontend jobs must report success; any step failure fails the PR

blockerFoundAndFixed.found: exit=2 with 16 TypeScript errors across 3 untracked scripts
blockerFoundAndFixed.verdict: PRE-EXISTING — these are the C2-R15 round-1/round-2 scripts, all untracked, so this typecheck failure would have blocked the PR with or without this round's work. It was never caught because the earlier local gates ran the specific scripts, not the repo-wide `npm run typecheck`.
blockerFoundAndFixed.rootCause: strict compiler options (noUncheckedIndexedAccess) on unchecked indexed access and regex capture groups: `args[0]`, `segments[0]`, `hops[i]`, `m[1]`, plus two over-narrow type declarations.
blockerFoundAndFixed.fix: type-only. Behaviour preserved, then verified: every fix either adds a runtime guard for a case that already fell through to the same result, or widens a declared type to what the code already accepts at runtime (`CoverageKind` -> `string`, which the resolver dispatches on and reports REGRESSION_COVERAGE_KIND_UNSUPPORTED for).

semanticReVerificationAfterFix.classification: 96 / 17 / 0 with authority agrees with resolver = true (unchanged)

loadSensitiveFlakes.lane: npm run test:contract (a test:ci member, so CI-gated)
loadSensitiveFlakes.observed: 2 of 12 cases failed in the full lane: 'traverses approved Typed Edges deterministically and matches NetworkX' (in-memory and in-process)
loadSensitiveFlakes.causeClass: load-sensitive, same class as the database flake. NetworkX 3.6.1 IS installed locally, so this is not a missing dependency.
loadSensitiveFlakes.constraint: Stage 9 / NetworkX are on the do-not-modify list — this must not be 'fixed' by editing the oracle or the test
loadSensitiveFlakes.evidenceQuality: weak causal link to this change; the file has no dependency on the reachability authority

loadSensitiveFlakes.observed: 2 of 3 cases failed in the full lane

localCiEquivalent results.test:database: 562 passed / 2 failed / 2 skipped earlier, all green on isolated rerun of the failing file

preExistingUncommittedProductionChanges.provenance: carried in the worktree from earlier C2-R15 rounds; NOT introduced by this round
preExistingUncommittedProductionChanges.relevanceToTheFlakes: none. There is no Ask-claim, knowledge-model or Stage 9 / NetworkX file in the list, and the two flaky files are concurrency/load sensitive.
preExistingUncommittedProductionChanges.note: the whole working tree is uncommitted, so no CI run can see ANY of this work yet — see the sequencing note

sequencingNote.observation: CI triggers on pull_request and on push to main. The branch codex/ts6-postgres-transaction-phase-b exists locally but nothing is committed or pushed, and the work order forbids commit/push/PR.
sequencingNote.consequence: there is no exact head for CI to verify until an owner-authorised commit + PR exists
sequencingNote.implication: the release gate cannot be reached inside these constraints; it needs owner authorisation to commit and push (or an explicit decision to run CI another way)

ciCoverageGap.finding: NO npm script and NO CI step runs scripts/ts6-audit/*. `test:ci` = unit, contract, integration, architecture, stage12-package only. `npm audit` is not the audit suite.
ciCoverageGap.consequence: the v6 lineage assertions added this round — 'derives the corrected v6 lineage and validates clean' and 'does not re-open an approved relation' — are NOT executed by CI. Neither is the qualified-authority scoreboard assertion. The owner's release checklist therefore depends on someone remembering to run them by hand.
ciCoverageGap.risk: the authority correction could silently drift without CI noticing
proposedOptionsNotApplied: add an npm script (e.g. `test:authority-audit`) and one CI step to run the two audit suites with an explicit timeout budget
or keep them manual and record the omission as an accepted limitation of the release gate
ciCoverageGap.whyNotApplied: a hard constraint forbids changing the test:contract policy and CI; adding a CI step needs explicit owner authorisation
